title: Consumables and Access Governance Workflow (Company-wide)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines a single, auditable workflow for provisioning consumable resources (software licenses, hardware peripherals, cloud service accounts), managing access and permissions across systems, handling non-trivial procurement and expenses, and governing vendor and travel processes for Redwood Inference. It is intended for managers, requesters, approvers, IT/Security, Purchasing, and People Ops.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and temporaries who require access to corporate systems or procurement of goods/services.
- Covers: identity & access lifecycle, change-control for privileged resources, procurement approvals, vendor onboarding & renewals, travel approvals and expense submission.

Core Principles

1) Least privilege by default. Grant only the minimum role required for the task.
2) Separation of duties. Approvers must not be the same as requesters or operational owners.
3) Short-lived elevated access. Emergency/privileged sessions are time-limited and logged.
4) Single source of truth. All requests must originate in the Request Portal and be linked to an approval record.
5) Periodic attestation. Access reviews occur on a defined cadence.

Roles and Ownership

- Requester: employee initiating a request (software, hardware, account, vendor engagement, travel).
- Line Manager: approves role necessity and budget alignment for purchases.
- IT/Access Team: performs provisioning/deprovisioning, maintains automation templates.
- Security: approves role mappings for privileged access and exception requests.
- Purchasing/Finance: executes vendor contracts, issues POs, processes invoices.
- People Ops: owner of policy, maintains training and role matrix.
- Vendor Owner (product/eng): day-to-day contact for vendor relationships.

Access & Permissions Lifecycle (standard workflow)

1) Request initiation
   - All requests must be submitted via the Request Portal (https://internal-requests.redwood.com). Choose the category: 'Access', 'Hardware', 'Software', 'Vendor', 'Travel', or 'Expense'.
   - Required fields: business justification, cost center, requested duration (if temporary), target systems, manager approval.

2) Automated pre-checks
   - The portal validates role templates, license availability, and existing entitlements. If a requested license exceeds allocation, purchasing workflow is triggered.

3) Approval path
   - Access <= 30 days and non-privileged: Line Manager approves.
   - Access > 30 days or privileged (admin, infra, billing, KMS): Manager + Security approval required.
   - New vendor engagements: Manager + Purchasing + Legal + Security (risk tier dependent).
   - Purchases under $2,500: Manager approval sufficient. $2,500–$50,000: Manager + Purchasing. >$50,000: Manager + Purchasing + Finance Director.

4) Provisioning
   - IT/Access Team performs provisioning via automation. For cloud/service accounts, use the standard naming convention: redwood-{env}-{team}-{resource}. Example SRE service account: redwood-prod-sre-monitoring-sa.
   - CLI example for sandbox service-account creation (internal tooling):
     $ rwdctl iam create-service-account --name redwood-dev-data-science-sa --roles "read-data, invoke-jobs" --expires 168h

5) Verification & Handover
   - Requester confirms access in the portal within 3 business days. If not confirmed, the ticket auto-escalates to IT/Access Team and Manager.

6) Periodic review & deprovisioning
   - Access attestation cadence:
     * Standard user roles: every 90 days.
     * Contractors & temps: every 30 days.
     * Privileged roles: monthly review.
   - Orphaned accounts identified by weekly audit; auto-suspend after 14 days of inactivity pending manual review.

Emergency Access & Exceptions

- For emergency access requests, submit an "Emergency Access" ticket and page the on-call Security engineer. Emergency grants are valid for a maximum of 4 hours and require a post-mortem and retrospective within 5 business days.
- Exceptions to least-privilege must include: scope, duration, business justification, owners, and compensating controls. Security will log the exception and assign an expiration.

Change Management (for production & privileged resources)

Purpose: Ensure controlled changes to services, infra, and high-risk configuration.

Change categories and required process:

- Minor (low risk, no customer impact): submit Change Request in CI/CD board, 2-day review SLA from SRE.
- Normal (scheduled, may impact internal users): Change Request -> Change Advisory Board (CAB) review weekly -> schedule maintenance window.
- Major (user-facing, cross-team, schema changes): Formal PRD + rollout plan + automated rollback + CAB + product approval.

Standard Change Request template (to use in the portal):
1) Change title and brief summary
2) Owner and rollback owner
3) Impacted systems and customers
4) Backout/rollback plan and automated health checks
5) Monitoring and observability runbook links
6) Validation steps and success criteria
7) Deployment window and stakeholders

Change validation checklist:
- Automated tests pass in staging and canary.
- Load baseline and smoke checks recorded.
- Rollback verified in a dry run.
- On-call rotation notified and coverage confirmed.

Data Management (high-level guidance)

- Data classification: Public, Internal, Restricted, Regulated. Default classification is Internal.
- Regulated data (PII, customer secrets, payment): require encryption at rest and in transit, limited access (Security + Data team approval), and retention schedule noted in the request.
- Data retention: follow department retention schedules; request a data-retention exception through Data Governance.
- Data deletion/transfer requests: submit Data Change ticket; include verification steps and audit trail.

Procurement & Expenses

Approval thresholds (summary):
- <$2500: Manager approval in Request Portal.
- $2,500–$50,000: Manager + Purchasing.
- >$50,000: Manager + Purchasing + Finance Director + Legal (if contract).

Purchase workflow:
1) Create purchase request (attach vendor quote + SOW if applicable).
2) Purchasing validates vendor, runs vendor risk check if tier > 1.
3) Purchasing issues PO and assigns payment terms.
4) On receipt, verify goods and close the ticket.

Expense submission (employees):
- Submit expenses in ExpenseApp within 10 business days. Attach receipts for amounts >= $25. Expenses > $500 require manager justification.

Sample procurement JSON template (paste into portal request if available):
{
  "title": "Purchase: 50 x JetBrains licenses",
  "cost_center": "ENG-PLATFORM",
  "estimated_total": "$7500",
  "vendor": "JetBrains",
  "justification": "Developer tooling standardization for Platform team",
  "required_by": "2026-04-01",
  "approvals": ["manager", "purchasing"]
}

Vendor Management & Onboarding

Tiering and required checks:
- Tier 1 (High risk): Vendors that store or process customer data or run within our VPC. Requirements: Security assessment, SOC2 or equivalent, contract review, SSO/SAML integration and quarterly security attestations.
- Tier 2 (Medium risk): Vendors that have access to internal systems but not regulated data. Requirements: Security questionnaire, contract + SLAs.
- Tier 3 (Low risk): Standard SaaS tools or office suppliers. Requirements: standard onboarding form and PO.

Vendor onboarding steps:
1) Requester opens Vendor Request in the portal and assigns a vendor owner.
2) Purchasing performs background checks and assigns tier.
3) Security performs risk assessment (Tier 1/2).
4) Legal reviews and signs contract.
5) IT completes necessary integrations (SSO, SCIM, network rules).

Renewal & offboarding:
- Vendors flagged for renewal 60 days before term end. Vendor owner files renewal packet: usage metrics, invoice forecast, security posture since last review, and recommended action (renew/terminate/renegotiate).
- Offboarding checklist includes removing SSO access, rotating credentials, terminating API keys, and confirming data deletion or retention instructions in writing.

Travel Policy (high level)

- Travel must be approved in advance via the Request Portal with manager sign-off. For international travel, People Ops must be looped for visa and travel safety guidance.
- Permissible expense categories: airfare (economy or flexible economy if >6h), lodging (mid-tier business), meals, ground transport, visa fees, and conference fees.
- Per diem and caps: consult the Travel Guidelines appendix in the portal; out-of-policy travel requires manager + People Ops approval.

Expense submission timeline:
- Submit travel expenses within 7 business days of trip completion. Late submissions require manager justification and People Ops review.

Templates and Forms (quick copy)

1) Access Request subject line: "Access Request: {team} - {resource} - {justification}"

2) Procurement brief template (one-paragraph for execs):
   - "What: (concise description)
     Why: (business outcome)
     Cost: (TCO over 12 months)
     Alternatives considered: (list)
     Owner: (product/eng owner)"

3) Vendor security checklist (yes/no):
   - Does the vendor have SOC2 or equivalent?
   - Is data encrypted at rest and in transit?
   - Are there shared credentials or API keys stored in plaintext?
   - Is there MFA and SSO support?

4) Change Request subject: "Change: {service} - {short description} - {deploy date}"

Escalation & SLA matrix

- Access request standard SLA: 3 business days for provisioning, 8 business days for purchases requiring PO.
- Emergency access: immediate pager, emergency grant <= 4 hours, retrospective within 5 business days.
- Vendor security review SLA: 10 business days (Tier 1), 5 business days (Tier 2).

Contacts and directories

- IT/Access Team: access-team@redwood.com (on-call rotation listed in the portal)
- Purchasing: purchasing@redwood.com
- Security (alerts): sec-ops@redwood.com
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com

Appendices

A. Access role naming conventions
- Roles: viewer, contributor, admin. Role string: {team}-{service}-{role}. Example: data-platform-bigquery-viewer.

B. Retention & audit logging
- All provisioning and deprovisioning actions are logged to the central audit stream for 7 years. Sensitive actions (privilege grants, exception approvals) include a JSON audit blob with reason, approver, TTL, and evidence link.

C. Change calendar governance
- Weekly CAB meeting: Wednesdays 09:00 PT. Schedule CAB requests by Monday 12:00 PT for that week. Major change blackout windows: end-of-quarter last 3 business days (unless explicitly approved by execs).

Document maintenance

- Owner (People Ops) must review this policy annually or when there are material process changes. All owners listed in this document must confirm compliance during quarterly ops reviews.

Revision history

- 2024-04-18: Document created by Asha Patel (People Ops)
- 2025-08-02: Added emergency access TTL and procurement thresholds (reviewers: Miguel Torres)
- 2026-02-10: Expanded vendor renewal workflow and added change calendar blackout guidance (reviewers: Lena Hofstad, Ravi Menon)

End of document
